title: Proper flat morphisms finite over a dense open are finite
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $U\subseteq S$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] whose underlying subset is dense, meaning that every nonempty open subset of $S$ meets $U$. Suppose that $X_U=X\times_S U\to U$ [def-pc-fibre-product] is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Then $f$ is finite.

proof.text: The assumed finite morphism $X_U\to U$ is quasi-finite by [pqf-lem-finite-qf], and by [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] a quasi-finite morphism is locally quasi-finite. By clause (3) of [pqf-def-quasifinite] a quasi-finite morphism is of finite type, hence locally of finite type in the sense of [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] (finite type is locally of finite type and quasi-compact), so [lem-trf-locally-quasi-finite-relative-dimension-zero] applies to $X_U\to U$. Its forward implication (locally quasi-finite implies relative dimension zero) gives $\dim_x((X_U)_{u})=0$ for every $x\in X_U$ with image $u\in U$; in particular $X_U\to U$ has relative dimension at most $0$.

source.place: Tag 0B48 proof, first sentence via Tag 081L; finite morphisms are quasi-finite by Tag 01TD/01TJ.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-flat-fp-relative-dimension-dense-open] with $e=0$. Its hypotheses are exactly the given flatness and local finite-presentation hypotheses on $f$, the density of $U$, and the bound of Step 1 for $X_U\to U$. Hence $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})\leq0$ for every $x\in X$. Since the point of $X_{f(x)}$ over $x$ lies in every open neighbourhood used in [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point], each such neighbourhood is nonempty and has dimension $\geq0$; so $\dim_x(X_{f(x)})=0$ for every $x\in X$, i.e. $f$ has relative dimension zero.

Since $f$ is proper, it is of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], hence locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. So the converse implication of [lem-trf-locally-quasi-finite-relative-dimension-zero] (relative dimension zero implies locally quasi-finite) applies to $f$ and, by Step 2, shows that $f$ is locally quasi-finite. Since $f$ is proper and locally quasi-finite, the Mathlib leaf [pqf-lem-proper-lqf-finite] gives that $f$ is finite.
